# InsertGo Website/Desktop integration context

Shared contract between Insert-Go Windows and Insert-Go Website. Identical mirror lives in both projects because workspace has no common Git worktree.

## System ownership

| Concern | Windows application | Website |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime | Tauri v2 / Rust 1.85 / React ^18.3.1 | Next.js ^15.3.8 / React ^19.0.0 |
| User interaction | Native palette, hotkeys, prompt flows | Browser login, approval, account, pricing |
| Authentication | Public native client; PKCE verifier/state; bearer token | Better Auth server; OAuth/OTP/SSO; session issuance |
| Secret storage | Session token in Windows Credential Manager | Auth, database, Gemini, email, billing secrets on server |
| AI generation | Sends prompt contract; consumes SSE | Authenticates, meters, debits, calls Gemini, streams SSE |
| Billing state | Displays server entitlements and opens checkout | Creates checkout; webhook updates PostgreSQL ledger |
| Durable data | Local settings/prompts plus one OS credential | PostgreSQL users, sessions, verification codes, quotas, credits |

Website is network authority. Desktop is public client. Desktop must never contain Better Auth secret, database credentials, OAuth client secret, billing secret, or Gemini API key.

## Base URL and environment contract

| Environment | Desktop | Website |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local | VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 | BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000 |
| Production | VITE_API_URL=https://insertgo.ai | BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://insertgo.ai |

Rules:

- VITE_API_URL and BETTER_AUTH_URL must identify same origin: scheme, host, and port.
- VITE_API_URL is compiled into desktop frontend. Never place secrets in any VITE_ variable.
- Desktop VITE_GEMINI_MODEL selects requested server model; Website GEMINI_API_KEY stays server-only.
- Website DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, OAuth secrets, Dodo secrets, and email secrets stay server-only.
- New Website origin must also be allowed by src-tauri/capabilities/default.json for opener and HTTP access.
- Tauri development origin is http://localhost:1420; Website Better Auth trustedOrigins must keep required Tauri origins.
- Google redirect remains BETTER_AUTH_URL/api/auth/callback/google.

## Native sign-in contract

Constants shared by both implementations:

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| client_id | insertgo-desktop |
| response_type | code |
| grant_type | authorization_code |
| code_challenge_method | S256 |
| redirect_uri | insertgo://auth/callback |
| authorization-code lifetime | 5 minutes |

Flow:

1. Desktop src/services/pkce.ts creates random verifier, S256 challenge, and CSRF state. Verifier stays memory-only.
2. Desktop src/store/authStore.ts installs deep-link listener before opening system browser.
3. Browser opens Website /desktop/authorize with client, redirect, challenge, method, response type, and state.
4. Website validates query. Unauthenticated users pass through /login and return to approval page.
5. User explicitly approves. POST /api/desktop/authorize requires same-origin browser request plus valid cookie session.
6. Website stores user id and challenge under random, single-use, five-minute code; browser navigates to callback with code and state only.
7. Tauri insertgo scheme returns callback to running app. Windows launches new process, so single-instance deep-link integration forwards event.
8. Desktop accepts exact callback URI and matching state, then POSTs code and verifier to /api/desktop/token.
9. Website atomically consumes code, verifies S256 using constant-time comparison, creates Better Auth session, and returns bearer token.
10. Desktop stores token under service InsertGo / account session in Windows Credential Manager, then calls /api/auth/get-session.

Never return session token through callback URI. Never persist verifier. Never log callback URL, authorization code, verifier, bearer token, or user prompt.

Known protocol gap: RFC 8252 recommends reverse-domain private URI schemes. Current insertgo scheme is already shipped and does not follow that naming form. PKCE prevents another scheme handler from redeeming an intercepted code, but does not prevent scheme collision. Any rename requires versioned dual-scheme migration across Website, Tauri config, installer registration, and deployed clients.

## HTTP contracts

### Desktop authorization

| Endpoint | Authentication | Request | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET /desktop/authorize | Browser cookie when signed in | PKCE query fields | Approval UI |
| POST /api/desktop/authorize | Browser cookie + same Origin | client_id, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, state | JSON redirect containing code + state |
| POST /api/desktop/token | Code + verifier | grant_type, client_id, code, code_verifier | access_token, token_type=Bearer, expires_in |
| GET /api/auth/get-session | Bearer token | None | Better Auth user/session plus entitlement fields |
| POST /api/auth/sign-out | Bearer token | Empty JSON object | Revoked server session |

### Managed AI relay

POST /api/ai/generate:

- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer session token.
- Retry identity: one Idempotency-Key per logical generation, reused across transport retries.
- JSON request: prompt, system, model, optional grounded boolean.
- Server validates session, raw-body size, prompt/system limits, burst quota, daily quota, and credits before Gemini call.
- Success: text/event-stream containing Gemini response frames; optional final grounding citation frame.
- Balance headers: x-credits-daily, x-credits-addon, legacy x-credits-remaining.
- 401: expired or invalid session; desktop signs out.
- 402: insufficient credits with authoritative balance; desktop opens upgrade path.
- 409: stale idempotency-key replay.
- 413: oversized body or prompt contract.
- 429: per-user rate limit.
- 503: server, database, quota, or upstream capacity failure.

Desktop src/services/aiProviders.ts owns request/retry/SSE parsing. Website app/api/ai/generate/route.ts owns authentication, validation, billing, Gemini access, and streaming. Prompt and response bodies must never enter logs.

### Billing and entitlements

- Desktop POSTs Bearer-authenticated selection to /api/billing/checkout and opens returned hosted URL in system browser.
- Website accepts only server catalog selectors; prices and product ids never come from client.
- Dodo webhook signature is verified over capped raw body before parsing or database writes.
- Webhook updates tier or grants add-on credits idempotently.
- Website lib/auth.ts customSession stamps tier, daily balance, add-on balance, and feature entitlements onto get-session.
- Desktop refreshStatus mirrors those server values. Server database remains source of truth.

## Transport and storage boundaries

- General cross-origin calls use Desktop src/services/http.ts: Tauri HTTP plugin in packaged app, browser fetch in web development.
- Streaming AI client uses Tauri HTTP directly in packaged app so SSE and retries remain controlled.
- Tauri capability allowlist must contain Website origin. WebView CSP alone does not grant plugin HTTP scope.
- Production API traffic must use HTTPS.
- Session token persists only in Windows Credential Manager. Browser-only development fallback uses sessionStorage with one-hour TTL.
- Profile/entitlement mirror uses sessionStorage. Local copies never override server authorization.
- PostgreSQL owns session, user, authorization-code, quota, credit, and webhook-derived billing state.

## Local startup

1. Website: apply supabase-auth-schema.sql and configure .env.local per DEV_SETUP.md.
2. Website: set BETTER_AUTH_URL and start npm run dev.
3. Desktop: copy .env.example to .env; set matching VITE_API_URL and VITE_GEMINI_MODEL.
4. Desktop: run npm run tauri:dev. Browser-only Vite mode cannot receive insertgo callback.
5. Sign in from Desktop, approve in system browser, then verify /api/auth/get-session and one streamed generation.

## Failure map

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Browser does not open | opener capability and copyable authorization URL |
| Login returns to wrong host or port | exact VITE_API_URL / BETTER_AUTH_URL origin match |
| Approval works but app never resumes | real Tauri build, insertgo scheme registration, deep-link and single-instance plugins |
| invalid_grant from token endpoint | expired/replayed code, wrong verifier, or interrupted sign-in attempt |
| Repeated 401 | expired/revoked bearer token or failed credential-store hydration |
| Packaged app network failure | Tauri HTTP capability allowlist and HTTPS certificate |
| 402 after generation request | server credit ledger; refresh account session |
| 503 from generation | Website database, quota gate, GEMINI_API_KEY, or upstream capacity |
| Checkout opens but plan stays old | Dodo webhook URL, secret, signature, event subscription, database update |

## Coordinated-change checklist

When changing connection contract:

1. Update server validation/response first, preserving backward compatibility when deployed Desktop clients exist.
2. Update Desktop consumer and friendly error mapping.
3. Update both .env.example files and DEV_SETUP.md when origin or required configuration changes.
4. Update Tauri capability allowlist when host changes.
5. Update tests: Desktop pkce.test.ts, http.test.ts, aiProviders.test.ts; Website desktopAuth.test.ts, entitlements.test.ts, usageLimit.test.ts, dodo.test.ts.
6. Update this template in scripts/sync-context.mjs; run npm run context:sync.
7. Test full real-app flow: browser approval, deep-link callback, token exchange, session refresh, SSE generation, credit update, logout.
